header.sector: AI infrastructure build-out (spans spenders, chips, power, materials)
header.title: Credit markets single out debt-reliant AI infrastructure borrowers as weak links

s01_bottom_line.text: CDS spreads on financing-dependent AI infrastructure borrowers have spiked (one weak issuer to 1,100 bps implying ~50% five-year default probability) while large cash-generative AI leaders (50-120 bps) and broad IG (~60 bps) remain comparatively contained, indicating a targeted reassessment of repayment risk for debt-reliant AI business models. ⟨cited figures: approximate; approximate, read from a chart⟩
The article suggests investors should distinguish AI issuers by their ability to finance investment, service debt and turn spending into cash flow rather than by the AI label.

The article identifies credit-market stress as concentrated in debt-reliant AI issuers with limited cash flow; it does not quantify an earnings or equity-valuation impact for any named company, only CDS pricing and implied default probabilities.
